newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Kirby says estimates reasonable.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Kirby says estimates reasonable.

text.p: Kirby Corp chief executive officer Joe Pyne said on Tuesday analysts' estimates that the company would earn $0.19 in the first quarter were within reason.
"I'm not uncomfortable with that (number)," he told Reuters after the marine transportation firm's annual meeting.
Pyne said flooding on the Mississippi River had hampered shipping operations and would have a "tangible effect" on earnings. Floods in 1993 knocked about $0.05 off earnings, he said.
The $0.19 figure was the mean estimate compiled by First Call. Kirby earned $0.20 a share in the first quarter of 1996.

Pyne said second quarter results would also be affected by the flooding, but less so because "things are getting better" on the Mississippi. He said he expected a complete return to normal river conditions by mid-May.
Kirby is the top tank barge company in the United States. It earned $1.05 a share on revenues of $391 million last year.
